scripts_used: test_cigna.py (used only to discover the real latestUpdatesListing.html index of monthly PDFs; not used for records)
scripts_read_but_not_used_for_final_data: test_cigna_evicore_msk.py (static eviCore MSK guideline reference PDF - no per-item dates, not an 'activity' feed)

test_cigna_policy_detail.py (per-policy Revision Details history for 4 named policies - real dated revisions, kept as a separate supplementary source, not merged into this file to avoid double-counting policies also present in the monthly update)
selection_rule: all valid parsed entries from the September 2026 Cigna Policy Updates PDF, sorted by effective_date descending, ties broken by policy_code descending, top 100 retained
limitations: Data covers only the single most-recently-published monthly bulletin (September 2026); it is NOT a rolling 'latest 100 across all time' feed. The real site publishes 45 monthly PDFs (Jan 2023-Sep 2026, confirmed live at latestUpdatesListing.html) that could be parsed with the same method for a longer time series if needed later.
This September 2026 bulletin alone already contained 169 valid, distinctly-parsed real activity entries (more than the 100 requested), so no other month was fetched for this deliverable.

31 of the 169 parsed entries had no explicit per-item date in their own comment text; for those, the document's own stated default ('Effective September 15, 2026, unless otherwise noted') was applied and is flagged via date_source='document_default_unless_noted'. This is verbatim text from the source document, not an estimate.

The PDF's table structure is flattened to plain text by pypdf with no column delimiters, so policy_name/comment boundaries were recovered heuristically (regex anchored on the New/Updated/Retired status token, scanning backward for a title-shaped phrase). Roughly 92/100 saved records have a clean parenthetical policy code; a handful of names may still include a stray trailing word or an internal duplicate title (e.g. two similarly-named consecutive drug policies) due to this heuristic - no numeric/date fields were fabricated to compensate.
comment_summary is truncated to 400 characters (marked with '...' when cut) and is a verbatim excerpt of the source PDF text, not a rewritten summary.

test_cigna_evicore_msk.py and test_cigna_policy_detail.py were run successfully against real, live Cigna URLs but excluded from this dataset because they are not 'latest activity' feeds (static guideline PDF; per-policy long-run revision history for only 4 named policies) - see report for their standalone real output.
No authentication or paywall was encountered on any of the 4 scripts' targets; all URLs are public static.cigna.com assets.
